title: Luke Bible Quiz - Chapter 14
description: Ten questions on Luke 14: the Sabbath healing, the lowest place at the feast, the great supper and counting the cost.

questions.text: What illness did the man in front of Jesus in the Pharisee's house have?
questions.explanation: The text says a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.

questions.text: What does he say about everyone who exalts himself?
questions.explanation: He says that everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

answers.text: He will be honored at the table
He will be given the best seat

questions.text: What does the host say to the guest who sat in the lowest place?
questions.explanation: He says that the host may tell that guest, "Friend, move up higher," and then he will be honored before all who sit at the table.

questions.text: Whom does he say to invite when you make a feast?
questions.explanation: He says that when you make a feast you should ask the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind.

answers.text: The poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind
Rich neighbors who can repay you

questions.text: In the parable, what did one of the invited men say he had bought and had to go try out?
questions.explanation: One of the invited men said he had bought five yoke of oxen and had to go try them out.

answers.text: A herd of pigs in the country
A fattened calf for a feast

questions.text: After the servant reported that there was still room, where did the lord send him?
questions.explanation: When the servant said there was still room, the lord sent him out into the highways and hedges to compel people to come in, so that his house might be filled.

answers.text: Into the streets and lanes of the city
To the homes of the rich neighbors

questions.text: What does he say a person should do first who wants to build a tower?
questions.explanation: He says that whoever wants to build a tower first sits down and counts the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it.

answers.text: Sit down and count the cost

questions.text: With how many does the king in the example consider meeting the king who comes against him with twenty thousand?
questions.explanation: He asks what king, going to war, will not first consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one who comes against him with twenty thousand.

questions.text: What does he say the king does while the other is still a great way off?
questions.explanation: He says the king sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.

answers.text: He builds a tower to defend his border
He counts his ten thousand soldiers again
He calls the multitude together for war
He sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace

questions.text: What does he say about salt that has become flat and tasteless?
questions.explanation: He says such salt is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out.

answers.text: It is fit for nothing and is thrown out
It can be mixed with fresh salt
It is still good for the soil
It is used to season the manure pile
